intended_object: A comparison isomorphism in the category of finite projective R-modules. It identifies the library's chosen ring-universe representative of P × Q with the product of the chosen representatives of P and Q. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation on `repr`.
explanation:
The definition is the composite linear equivalence repr(P×Q) ≃ P×Q ≃ repr P × repr Q, made into a categorical isomorphism with `isoOfLinearEquiv`. It is built correctly: it chains `reprEquiv` for P × Q with `prodCongr` of the inverse `reprEquiv`s for P and Q. The target `of R (repr R P × repr R Q)` is a valid finite projective object.

The isomorphism depends on the non-canonical choice of representative made by `Module.Finite.repr`. It is bookkeeping data for the library's own API, comparing chosen representatives under products, and not a notion from the literature. Mathematically it only says that the representative of a direct sum is isomorphic to the sum of the representatives. So it is an auxiliary device rather than a mathematical object to formalize. Generality is not an issue: it works over any ring and with independent carrier universes.
